name: Shape Kingdom Nen
description: Shape and validate collective KAKIN capabilities as bounded, rights-aware Agent Skills with visible authority, Guardian, cost, refusal, verification, and KARMA contracts.

practice.ten: Hold the XENIA rights floor, declared scope, provenance, schema, and authority boundary throughout design and validation.
practice.zetsu: Refuse activation or let the ability rest when adoption, authority, a bounded budget, or a checkable outcome is absent.
practice.ren: Use only local read and bounded design effort unless a separately authorized effect is named.
practice.hatsu: Produce a KAKIN-suite Agent Skill and closed ability manifest whose limits and aftermath can be inspected before use.

requires: A named outcome, bearer scope, explicit effect boundary, and rights-preserving refusal path.
A repository declaration before a collective ability becomes active.
refuses: Personality typing, coerced adoption, hidden telemetry, a rights waiver, unbounded power, or an authority claim derived from the manifest.

vows.promise: Classify affinity and Guardian controls only from declared operations and effects.
vows.amplifies: Technical clarity without reducing a bearer to an inferred type.

vows.promise: Report validation as structural evidence and never as permission, consent, safety, or truth.

costs.limit: One coherent manifest and its direct references per shaping pass.
costs.recovery: Return a proposal with open questions; rest or resume without penalty.

costs.limit: Seek input only when a missing choice would materially change bearer scope, effects, or adoption.
costs.recovery: Keep the ability proposed until the relevant collaborator can respond.

checks: Closed schema, folder and skill parity, duplicate keys, adoption rules, support files, and symlink boundaries.
guardian.budget: Offline schema, parity, symlink, adoption, and deterministic semantic checks under a 64 KiB per-file inspection cap.
guardian.retention: Keep only command output deliberately captured by the invoker; the validator stores nothing.
recipients: The local invoker receives stdout and stderr; no telemetry or data leaves the process.
guardian.uncertainty: Structural validation does not prove consent, identity, permission, safety, behavior, or truth.
guardian.stop: The invoker can stop validation at any time; the sidecar performs no skill execution or external effect.
guardian.appeal: Challenge a diagnostic with the schema, fixture, and canonical input; revise the contract rather than scoring the bearer.
guardian.repair: Correct the schema, manifest, validator, or diagnostic and rerun without changing bearer standing.

effects: Creates or reviews local skill instructions, manifests, schemas, and deterministic validation evidence.
externalities: A rigid taxonomy can obscure difference if treated as personality or authority; the skill explicitly rejects that use.
returns: Suite-versioned artifacts, separate manifest and full-bundle digests, diagnostics without rejected values, and a repair path.
repair: Keep source material, revise or retire the proposal, correct attribution, and record any affected participant's concern without retaliation.

allows: Read named local design inputs and create or validate local Nen skill artifacts within the requested workspace.
forbids: Invent identity, adoption, consciousness, consent, authority, or a universal truth verdict.
requires_permission: External publication, deployment, messages, purchases, credential changes, private-resource access, paid inference, or production mutation.

checks: Run the central closed-schema validator and isolated Nen protocol tests.
Run Skill Creator validation and forward-test realistic positive and refusal prompts.
